reason: E1 supports the premise that Al2O3 is an excellent oxygen barrier up to ~1300°C, but it does not address pack cementation or refractory HEAs. E2 shows that increasing Al content in a different alloy system (CoCrNiAlX) promotes a dense Al2O3 scale and reduces oxidation, but it does not involve pack cementation or refractory HEAs. The premises about pack cementation effectiveness and the baseline oxide behavior of untreated refractory HEAs are not supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Al2O3 is an excellent oxygen barrier with low diffusivity up to ~1300°C
Pack cementation can increase surface Al concentration in alloys
Higher Al content promotes formation of a continuous, dense Al2O3 scale
A continuous Al2O3 scale reduces oxidation rate by blocking oxygen ingress and metal cation outward diffusion
Untreated refractory HEAs form mixed, less protective oxides (e.g., Cr-based, CrTaO4)
